knowledge:
- key_parameters: type="fastq" in qa() to specify the file format for QA statistics ;; colClasses in readXStringColumns() to specify the class of each column to be read (e.g., "DNAString", "BString") or NULL to ignore ;; destination in writeFastq() to specify the output file path ;; mode="a" in writeFastq() to append reads to the destination file during chunk-wise iteration.
- alternatives: For BAM files or aligned reads, use Rsamtools, GenomicRanges, GenomicAlignments, and related packages instead of ShortRead's legacy alignment functions ;; For whole-genome alignments or more flexible pairwise alignment, use Biostrings and pwalign (specifically PDict, matchPDict, and pairwiseAlignment) instead of srdistance.
- when_to_use: Use when you have raw FASTQ files from high-throughput sequencing and need to perform initial quality control, generate visual QA reports, or filter/trim reads (e.g., removing low-quality tails, adapter sequences, or reads with too many ambiguous bases) before downstream alignment.
- pitfalls: Reading entire large FASTQ files into memory with readFastq can exhaust system memory; use FastqStreamer to iterate in chunks or FastqSampler to sample ;; When filtering or trimming paired-end reads, care must be taken to coordinate pairs of FASTQ files to preserve read order ;; srdistance is optimized for reference sequences of similar length to the reads; for whole-genome or highly flexible alignments, it is inefficient compared to Biostrings tools.

workflows.name: fastq_quality_assessment
workflows.intent: Generate an HTML quality assessment report from a set of FASTQ files.
workflows.stages: 1. List FASTQ files using dir() ;; 2. Collect QA statistics over the files using qa() ;; 3. Generate and view the HTML report using report() and browseURL()
workflows.code:
fls <- dir("/path/to", "*fastq$", full=TRUE)
qaSummary <- qa(fls, type="fastq")
browseURL(report(qaSummary))

workflows.name: fastq_filtering_and_trimming
workflows.intent: Iterate through a FASTQ file in chunks to filter out low-quality reads and trim low-quality ends.
workflows.stages: 1. Open a stream to the FASTQ file using FastqStreamer() ;; 2. Yield chunks of reads using yield() ;; 3. Filter reads using nFilter() or custom filters ;; 4. Trim low-quality nucleotides using trimTailw() ;; 5. Filter by read length using width() ;; 6. Append processed reads to a destination file using writeFastq()
workflows.code:
myFilterAndTrim <-
    function(fl, destination=sprintf("%s_subset", fl))
{
    ## open input stream
    stream <- open(FastqStreamer(fl))
    on.exit(close(stream))
    repeat {
        ## input chunk
        fq <- yield(stream)
        if (length(fq) == 0)
            break
        ## trim and filter, e.g., reads cannot contain 'N'...
        fq <- fq[nFilter()(fq)]  # see ?srFilter for pre-defined filters
        ## trim as soon as 2 of 5 nucleotides has quality encoding less
        ## than "4" (phred score 20)
        fq <- trimTailw(fq, 2, "4", 2)
        ## drop reads that are less than 36nt
        fq <- fq[width(fq) >= 36]
        ## append to destination
        writeFastq(fq, destination, "a")
    }
}

workflows.name: parsing_custom_tabular_sequence_files
workflows.intent: Read specific columns of sequence and quality data from tabular text files (e.g., Solexa export format) into Biostrings objects.
input: s_2_export.txt (tabular text file containing sequence and quality columns)
workflows.stages: 1. Define column classes using a list where target columns are specified as "DNAString" or "BString" and others are NULL ;; 2. Read the specified columns from the file using readXStringColumns()
workflows.code:
colClasses <- rep(list(NULL), 21)
colClasses[9:10] <- c("DNAString", "BString")
names(colClasses)[9:10] <- c("read", "quality")
cols <- readXStringColumns(analysisPath(sp), pattern, colClasses)
